PullRequest.Title: Enhance TypeScript 7 API with SDK support and connection tests
PullRequest.Body: Introduce support for TypeScript 7 extensions and implement tests to verify connection behavior with various language servers. This enhancement ensures compatibility with the TypeScript 7.1 API and improves the overall SDK functionality.

Scenarios.Scenario: First TypeScript 7 feature use and initial context-provider registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration awaits extension activation and isActivated(), which awaits the shared API connection. Connection establishment awaits subscription, SDK pipe initialization, and API.fromLSPConnection. Construction alone does not connect.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate candidate TypeScript extensions through the extension API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three activation calls during a discovery pass, stopping at the first usable extension API; no repeated activation after subscription succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Activated only the first installed candidate. The diff adds a bounded fallback for SDK-only extensions, not document- or workspace-size fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before first connection; already-active extensions reuse VS Code activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request an API pipe from the selected SDK and connect using API.fromLSPConnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one initialization/connect pair per shared connection generation, zero on warm successful calls or unsupported SDKs; up to three sequential attempts if the server changes while connecting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Requested a pipe from the extension API and used the same API.fromLSPConnection boundary with the same three-attempt bound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks initial feature availability, not general extension construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to three fixed extension IDs, stopping at the first event-providing extension; all four native-API consumer types share one connection rather than connecting per document or consumer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Extension activation is sequential within discovery; one connection-creation promise is shared globally. At most three sequential connection attempts handle generation changes, preserving the existing attempt bound.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Concurrent getApi calls share apiPromise; successful connections are cached. Subscription is cached independently. A subscribed server with an absent or unsupported SDK returns undefined without pipe initialization. If no extension exposes an API, later calls rescan the bounded extension list; retrying discovery after an unsuccessful attempt also existed before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: connection sharing, promise coalescing, fixed extension inventory, version gating, and retry bounds are explicit in the implementation and covered by the added connection tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External extension activation and pipe setup durations are not available in the repository. No input-dependent increase beyond the intentional fixed fallback is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: lazy shared connection creation and bounded sequential discovery remain intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Late language-server initialization, server restart, and provider re-registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initialization updates the SDK, resets the connection, clears context state, and queues checkRegistration. Registration waits for a shared replacement connection before replacing registrations. This runs on server initialization, not on each edit or context item.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close a stale API connection and establish a replacement pipe when requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cached connection close per reset and one shared replacement connection in the ordinary restart case; stale in-progress attempts are closed and retries are bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reset/close and generation-based replacement already existed. Notifications previously required an established API; the diff additionally allows consumers that previously found no API to retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replacement connection establishment precedes restored provider availability; closing is asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the cache-population inline completion provider and unregister its previous handle when replacing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per successful queued registration check, plus one unregistration when replacing an existing registration. Internal context-provider registration adds one removable array entry, not one per target or document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These registration operations occurred on initial checks and relevant configuration changes; server initialization now also schedules a check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after successful activation; restores the provider after late initialization or restart.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure the selected TypeScript extension and optional legacy Copilot extension are activated before registering their providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One TypeScript activation lookup and at most one legacy Copilot activation lookup per registration check; VS Code reuses existing extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helpers were used for initial and configuration-triggered registration; the new activation event adds this bounded registration trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the serialized registration task.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event subscription per shared connection and one activation-forwarding chain for the context service; work scales with actual server initialization events, not open files or symbols.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The registration Queue has parallelism one. Connection creation is separately coalesced through apiPromise. Old provider registrations are disposed before replacements, and service event listeners are cleared on service replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each server initialization invalidates the API and runnable cache intentionally. An SDK replay during initial subscription does not emit a reconnect notification. Existing pending connection work remains coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event path, queue implementation, registry cleanup, and extension-host registration IPC were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Restart frequency and external activation durations are unknown. There is no evidence of an event feedback loop, per-file fan-out, or accumulating registrations.
Scenarios.Verdict: The additional bounded work restores registration on actual server lifecycle changes; no high-confidence performance bug is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing, cursor selection, cache population, and inline completion context resolution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing selection/completion triggers populate context asynchronously. Population obtains the shared API, creates a snapshot, reads the project/source, computes context, and disposes the snapshot. Completion resolution primarily yields cached results and can race in-flight population for at most 20 ms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a native snapshot, obtain the default project and source file, perform native context queries, and dispose the snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot lifecycle per actual population request, with query count controlled by existing context computation and budgets. No new query loop or changed payload is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot, project/source lookup, computation, disposal, and completion race existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for fresh cache population; foreground completion waits on an existing request only through the unchanged bounded race.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active-document selection/completion events and requested context size; not all workspace documents. One in-flight population request plus the latest pending request is retained.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing throttled selection handling and in-flight population suppression remain. All feature callers coalesce connection creation; completed-context reads do not create independent connections.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm API calls do not reconnect. Runnable-result cache use is unchanged. With a subscribed unsupported or not-yet-initialized SDK, getApi does no pipe work. Failed connection attempts can be retried on later calls, as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: population triggers, cancellation, pending-request handling, and cached completion consumption are explicit in the surrounding code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual native-query duration depends on project size, but this diff does not increase steady-state query cardinality or change budgets.
Scenarios.Verdict: No steady-state hot-path regression: changed connection handling preserves caching and request coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Region lookup, structural diff, and next-edit-suggestion rename using the shared API
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each feature awaits getApi and then its existing native snapshot/query lifecycle. Region lookup shares one snapshot and source file across requested ranges. Structural diff reads original and modified content in temporary snapshots; rename queries the current project/source before analysis.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/dispose one snapshot and fetch the document's project and source file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot/project/source lookup sequence for the entire ranges array, not one per range.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical feature-level native calls and grouping; only shared connection discovery/version validation changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before returning the requested regions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a snapshot, perform two temporary text-update/source-read sequences, dispose, and close the opened file through another snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two temporary document versions per diff request and the existing opening/closing snapshot lifecycles, independent of changed-line count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical snapshot and temporary-update operations existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by structural-diff generation, including existing cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/dispose a snapshot, fetch project/source state, and execute existing native rename analysis.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot lifecycle per prepare or postRename call, with unchanged analysis-dependent query counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-request native analysis boundaries; no added per-symbol connection or initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Requested ranges within one document, the two structural-diff document versions, and rename query scope. These consumers share the same connection as language context.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection establishment is globally coalesced, not per consumer. Feature operations retain their existing concurrency; the diff adds no Promise.all fan-out or new limiter bypass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: One cached API serves all consumers. Unsupported SDKs return no API without connecting; successful requests preserve existing source-cache clearing and per-request snapshot disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all production TypeScript7Api consumers were located and their connection usage and snapshot ownership inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native server internals and operation timings are external; the reviewed code supplies no evidence that the SDK metadata changes per-request work on supported servers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression: connection compatibility changes do not multiply these existing expensive paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switching TypeScript versions or disabling support, then disposing services
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration changes dispose the previous language-context service and rebind listeners. Disposing the last native-API handle closes the shared connection; closing is asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close the shared native API connection when its final handle is disposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One close for the cached connection when the last handle is removed; no close per document or per remaining handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reference-counted disposal and asynchronous close mechanism existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup is initiated without awaiting API.close.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configuration transitions and a fixed set of service handles, rather than document history or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing ref counting owns connection lifetime. New event emitters and subscriptions are owned by DisposableStores; no additional background task or unbounded retained collection is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared connection persists only while reference-counted handles remain. Subscription disposal removes the server listener; serviceListeners.clear removes forwarded listeners before replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership of each added emitter and listener is explicit and replacement clears the old forwarding store.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured retained sizes are available, but no lost disposal owner or growing collection is present in the changed code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup or retention regression found.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and every diff page in the performance-review pass. Traced shared API consumers, startup/late initialization, restart registration, steady-state context work, and disposal. No concrete diff-introduced performance issue or independently evidenced shipped performance-regression fix met the reporting standard.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
